### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/bin/objectstack-scenarios.js`, `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/bin/objectstack-scenarios.js`, `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4038ec7671497ba5f367ae96fd7ebe045e94fee5` — the merge of head `149e988b3ca2d98395b92638c7143bb3fd9af102` into base `065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4038ec7671497ba5f367ae96fd7ebe045e94fee5 && git checkout 4038ec7671497ba5f367ae96fd7ebe045e94fee5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596 149e988b3ca2d98395b92638c7143bb3fd9af102 && git checkout -B drift-repro 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596 && git merge --no-ff 149e988b3ca2d98395b92638c7143bb3fd9af102

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 065bba721e4ba180c6bdbbf2c5fb787d49bac596` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `149e988b3ca2d98395b92638c7143bb3fd9af102`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration. The committed tree holds no published spec schema and no governed path; the PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Inputs read: card #31172 (body and all five comments, newest os-dev-report 6711888045), PR #31221 (body, 14-file list, three-dot diff against `main` at the merge base `065bba72`), and the 71 check-runs on this head. Every completed check-run concluded `success` or `skipped` (the skips are label- or path-gated jobs: Pack Smoke opt-in without `needs:pack-smoke`, Build Docs, UI lanes, the 18.x harness); none is `failure`, `neutral` or `cancelled`. Test Core 8/8 shards plus the aggregate, Check Changeset (both the push run and the `edited` run), Lint and Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Validate Package Dependencies and PR-body guards are green. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run here. The committed tree was read with `git show` and `git grep` at the head only.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong:

1. **Private to published** (`packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`): `private: true` removed; `publishConfig.access: public`, `files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]`, `engines.node 22 or later` are byte-for-byte the fields of `packages/verify/package.json`, and `engines` matches the root manifest. Right. `CHANGELOG.md` does not yet exist in the package (same as every first release in this train: npm skips a missing `files` entry and `changeset version` writes it); informational only.
2. **`exports` keys unchanged**: `.`, `./export`, `./runner`, `./score`, `./score/full`, the five the PR body table names. The two new build entries `bin` (`src/bin.ts`) and `cli` (`src/runner/cli.ts`) are not `exports` keys, so `dist/bin.js` and `dist/cli.js` resolve for no consumer; `src/runner/index.ts` re-exports eleven modules and neither `cli.js` nor `library.js`; `src/export/index.ts` does not re-export `export/cli.ts`. The PR body's public-surface claim is right.
3. **The `objectstack-scenarios` bin** (`bin.objectstack-scenarios` to `./bin/objectstack-scenarios.js`): the entry imports only `../dist/bin.js` (built JavaScript, card ask 4). `runCli` dispatches `run` to the runner's own `main` with the remaining argv untouched (card ask 1: today's `run-scenarios` options, no second flag table), `help`/`--help`/`-h` and `version`/`--version`/`-v` exit 0, no or unknown command exits 2 with the usage on stderr. The file sits outside `files[]`, which is fine: npm and pnpm pack always include the `bin` target, and `packed-tarball.test.ts` asserts `bin/objectstack-scenarios.js` is in the tarball. The tsup plugin `binLoadsBuiltCli` externalises exactly `./runner/cli.js` imported from `bin.ts` to `./cli.js` (or `./cli.cjs`), so `help`/`version` never load the runner graph; `shims: true` is set, so the `import.meta.url` in both `.cjs` emissions is shimmed and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (which parses every `dist/**/*.cjs`) is green. The runner CLI's self-run guard compares `argv[1]` with its own module URL, so it never fires under the bin. Right.
4. **The packaged card library under `dist/library`** (`scripts/pack-library.mjs`): copies exactly two directories of this repository, `docs/qa/scenarios` and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas`, one level deep, regular `.json` files only, after `rmSync` of the target, and exits 1 if either is empty. The private overlay (cloud#3603) has no path in this repository, so nothing can reach the copy by construction, and `packed-tarball.test.ts` refuses any JSON that is not `package.json` or byte-identical to an open card or area, and pins every shipped card `origin: generic` (card ask 2). `src/runner/library.ts` `locateLibraryRoot` recognises a checkout only when the package sits at `packages/qa/scenarios` of a pnpm workspace holding `docs/qa/scenarios`, compared by real path, else answers the packed copy or throws when it is absent; `libraryOf` (unchanged) therefore reads the shipped copy as `open` and any `--cards` directory as the overlay. `cli.ts` now uses it in place of `findUp(pnpm-workspace.yaml)`, defaults `--out` to `./scenario-runs` off a checkout, stamps no framework commit off a checkout, and refuses `--packages workspace` off a checkout before `mkdirSync` of the work or out directory. The exporter CLI (`src/export/cli.ts`) still uses `findUp`, but it is reachable from npm through no `exports` key and no bin, so nothing is owed. Right.
5. **What `files[]` ships**: `dist` (the five subpath entries, `bin.js`, `cli.js`, their `.cjs`, `.d.ts`, sourcemaps without `sourcesContent`, and `dist/library/**`), `README.md`, and the `bin` target; the tarball test pins no `.ts` source, no `src/`, `test/` or `scripts/`, no `workspace:` range left in the manifest. Right.
6. **`.changeset/config.json`**: `@objectstack/scenarios` added to the `fixed` group after `@objectstack/verify`, so it versions with the `@objectstack/*` train and nothing is bumped by hand (`check:changeset-fixed` green). Right.
7. **`packages/spec/llms.txt`** 74 to 75: `packages/spec/scripts/check-llms-txt.ts` re-derives the package-ecosystem count against the real non-private `@objectstack/*` workspace packages, so publishing this one moves it by exactly one; the gate is green on this head. Right, and correctly named in the PR body as gate-derived fallout outside the claimed surface.
8. **`packages/qa/scenarios/turbo.json`**: adds both library directories to the build's inputs with `$TURBO_EXTENDS$`, so a card edit invalidates the cached build the release would otherwise replay; the root `@objectstack/scenarios#test` task already depends on the package's own `build` and lists the same globs, so `dist/` exists before `packed-tarball.test.ts` runs (`check:turbo-task-graph`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:ci-filter-parity` green). Right.
9. **Card ask 3** (runner rules kept): the API-billed refusal is untouched pre-existing driver code and is smoke-pinned from the packed bin; `--packages published` stays the default; the exporter's `workspace` refusal is #31188's and lives in `./export`. Right.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/31172-publish-scenarios-cli.md` grades `@objectstack/scenarios` at `patch` and carries both declaration lines. Under AGENTS.md §3 the level follows the kind alone: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, a `feat:` and a widening alike; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `none` with `minor` on any package ("A `minor` is earned by a change to the metadata protocol and by nothing else"). The diff adds no authorable key, value or metadata type (a package becoming public, a bin, package data and a repository-vs-install path switch), so `none` is the right kind and `patch` the right level; Check Changeset is green on this head and was red on the earlier `minor`. The card's ask 5 said `minor`; the repo rule supersedes the card's wording and the dev's deviation names it. `Clause-②: yes` is right: the diff widens the public surface (a published package and a command) and removes nothing a consumer or author could reach, so no `(narrowing)` arm applies; `yes` with no arm is a permitted form. Nothing moves `@objectstack/spec`'s schema, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

From the os-dev-report comments (6711207780 round 1, 6711888045 round 2, newest):

- **`packages/spec/llms.txt` outside the claimed surface** — answered: gate-derived (①7), one count line, named in the PR body; accepted as same-class fallout.
- **Changeset `minor` to `patch`** — answered (②): the gate's rule, not a dodge; `Check Changeset` green.
- **PR body not PATCHed by the dev** — answered: the body on the PR is the round-2 body (cites `149e988b`, `patch`, 10 tarball cases, the seat trailer as its last line, and the body-reading `edited` run of Check Changeset is green).
- **Triage ⚠️ asked for a tarball check in the publish job; `release.yml` not edited** — answered, with a should-fix: the leak check is the Test Core allow-list, which runs on every PR and in the merge queue, so a leak is red before a release commit exists; the release pipeline is outside the claimed surface and the Publish Smoke workflow already smokes the release candidate's tarballs after Release. A release-time `npm pack --dry-run` guard for this package is a follow-up card if the maintainer wants it, not a condition of this PR.
- **Test budget: three `run` spawn cases at an explicit 30 s each; no file `test-budget` header; CI file reading NOT MEASURED** — answered: `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` requires a header only when the measurement window reads the file above the 10 s line; it reads 5.1 s locally and Test Core is green on this head. If a later window lists it, the header is the refresh lane's, as the report says.
- **Round-1 out-of-scope finding, `node dist/bin.js run` tripping the runner's self-run guard** — answered: gone in round 2, `dist/bin.js` has no top-level effect and the guard lives in `dist/cli.js`, whose `argv[1]` under the bin is `bin/objectstack-scenarios.js`.
- **`open_questions`: []** in both rounds; `security_findings: none`; the premise (`private: true`, no `bin` on `main`) still holds on the merge base.

Nothing escalates. Should-fix only (non-blocking, follow-up carriers): the release-time tarball guard above.
